processing: A cultivar, not a finished tea. It has been judged suitable for green tea, and one nursery also recommends it for black and white tea.
harvest_season: An early-budding cultivar, used like other early plants for spring picking. In a Xinyang trial it budded about when Fuding Dabai did.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea made from it; the Baihao name refers to white down on the young shoots.
appearance_liquor: Made as a green tea, typically a clear yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Medium-sized leaf; made as a green tea, typically soft and green.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting description is recorded; made as a green tea, expect the fresh, vegetal and sweet cup typical of Sichuan greens.

brewing.notes: A general method for green tea; brew for whatever style was made from the leaf.

vintage_note: Normally a plant name for growers and is rarely named on retail tea. Green tea from it follows the usual rule for its class: the current spring's harvest, drunk within about a year.
description:
Mingshan 131, also called Mingshan Baihao, is a clonal tea cultivar associated with Mingshan near Ya'an in Sichuan. It is a shrub with medium-sized leaves and an early start to the season, and it is diploid.

Its practical appeal is yield. In a trial around Xinyang in Henan it out-yielded the standard Fuding Dabai while budding about the same time, and was judged good for green tea and worth planting in that region.

Flavour is less well recorded. The notes here on the cup are what is typical of Sichuan green tea rather than a tasting of this plant.

You will mostly meet it in garden lists rather than on a tea shelf. If a seller names it, ask what style they made from it.
history:
Its parentage and breeders are not clearly recorded. A British tea-plant nursery gives its origin as Ya'an and a registration in 2005; this is a trade account, not an official record.

A 2004 study of Mingshan Baihao already treated it as a newly bred cultivar when testing it in Henan.
